textbookText: 91. The derivative of a function f(x) at a point represents: A) The instantaneous rate of change of the function (the slope of the tangent line) at that point B) The total area under the curve up to that point C) The average value of the function over an interval D) The value of the function itself at that point
92. The derivative of xⁿ with respect to x is: A) nxⁿ⁻¹ B) xⁿ⁻¹ C) nxⁿ⁺¹ D) nxⁿ
93. The derivative of a constant is: A) Zero B) The constant itself C) One D) Undefined
94. The derivative of sin x with respect to x is: A) cos x B) −cos x C) −sin x D) tan x
95. The derivative of cos x with respect to x is: A) −sin x B) sin x C) −cos x D) sec²x
96. The derivative of eˣ with respect to x is: A) eˣ itself (a unique property: its own derivative) B) x·eˣ⁻¹ C) eˣ⁻¹ D) x·eˣ
97. The derivative of ln x (natural log) with respect to x is: A) 1/x B) x C) ln x itself D) 1/x²
98. The Product Rule for differentiation of u(x)·v(x) states: A) d/dx(uv) = u'v + uv' B) d/dx(uv) = u'v' C) d/dx(uv) = u' + v' D) d/dx(uv) = (u'v − uv')

99. The Chain Rule is used to differentiate: A) A composite function, e.g., f(g(x)), by multiplying f'(g(x)) with g'(x) B) Only sums of two functions C) Only constant functions D) Only functions with no variable at all
100. Integration is fundamentally the reverse (inverse) process of: A) Differentiation B) Multiplication C) Addition D) Taking limits
101. ∫xⁿ dx (for n ≠ −1) equals: A) xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C B) nxⁿ⁻¹ + C C) xⁿ⁻¹/(n−1) + C D) xⁿ + C

102. The definite integral ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx geometrically represents: A) The net (signed) area under the curve y = f(x) between x = a and x = b B) The slope of the tangent to f(x) at x = a C) The value of f(x) at x = b only D) The average rate of change of f(x) at a single point

103. A limit lim(x→a) f(x) describes: A) The value that f(x) approaches as x gets arbitrarily close to a B) The exact value of f(a) always, with no distinction from continuity C) The derivative of f(x) at x = a D) The integral of f(x) from 0 to a

104. A function f(x) is continuous at x = a if: A) lim(x→a) f(x) exists and equals f(a) B) f(x) is differentiable everywhere, regardless of limits C) f(a) is undefined D) The function has a jump/break at x = a

105. The second derivative of a function is used to determine: A) The concavity of the curve and to identify points of inflection B) Only the slope of the tangent, same as the first derivative C) The x-intercepts of the function D) The domain of the function

106. At a local maximum of a differentiable function, the first derivative: A) Equals zero, and the second derivative is negative (concave down) B) Is always positive C) Is always negative D) Is undefined
107. At a local minimum of a differentiable function, the second derivative is generally: A) Positive (concave up) B) Negative (concave down) C) Zero always D) Undefined
108. The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links: A) Differentiation and integration as inverse operations B) Limits and continuity only C) Vectors and scalars D) Complex numbers and real numbers

109. Which of the following extraordinary historical facts about calculus is TRUE? A) Calculus was independently developed by both Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz in the late 17th century B) Calculus was invented solely by Pythagoras in ancient Greece C) Calculus has no application in physics, only in pure abstract mathematics D) Integration was discovered after computers, in the 20th century
110. The derivative of tan x with respect to x is: A) sec²x B) cos²x C) −sec²x D) cot x
111. Applying the Quotient Rule to differentiate u(x)/v(x) gives: A) (u'v − uv')/v² B) (u'v + uv')/v² C) u'/v' D) (uv' − u'v)/v²
112. ∫(1/x) dx equals: A) ln|x| + C B) 1/x² + C C) x·ln x + C D) −1/x² + C

113. The derivative of xⁿ at a critical point where the derivative equals zero indicates: A) A possible local maximum, minimum, or point of inflection (needs further testing) B) That the function is undefined there C) That the function has no value at that point D) That the function must be increasing there

114. Application of calculus in physics: velocity is defined as: A) The derivative of displacement with respect to time B) The integral of displacement with respect to time C) The second derivative of time with respect to displacement D) A constant, unrelated to displacement

115. Application of calculus: acceleration is defined as: A) The derivative of velocity with respect to time (or the second derivative of displacement) B) The integral of velocity with respect to time C) The same as velocity, just renamed D) Independent of time entirely

116. An indefinite integral always includes: A) An arbitrary constant of integration, "+C", since infinitely many antiderivatives differ by a constant B) Fixed upper and lower limits C) No constant term at all D) Only even-powered terms
